**Verdict: PASS** for DG1 round 4 (task T-DG1-REV-DOM-R4) on candidate `sha256:6e0c0db1a8bea33cd81f05ea8c795d8ede4bfb7f380dfe146556cb4875a6f827`. There are no new findings and nothing is regressed.

**Candidate check:** `git rev-parse HEAD` is `91936e6`. Recomputing the candidate ID gives the same value with 395 files, both in the repo (Node 24) and in a disposable clone (Node 22). Compared with round 3, only two files changed: `apps/web/package.json`, whose `typecheck` script now also runs the new `tsconfig.e2e.json`, and that new `apps/web/tsconfig.e2e.json` (F-DG1-147). Nothing in the source documents or in the shared, web, API or database code changed.

**Checks (all run in a disposable clone):**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm -r typecheck` | PASS; the apps/web step now also runs `tsc -p tsconfig.e2e.json` |
| Test of the F-DG1-147 fix: add a type error to `journeys.spec.ts`, run typecheck, revert | PASS; it failed with TS2322 (exit 2), then passed after the revert |
| `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm lint` | PASS |
| `pnpm test`, Node 22 and Node 24 | PASS on both, 326/326 tests |
| `check:contrast` | PASS |
| No-CDN scan, OpenAPI lint, search for official PMI/Mobily claims | PASS; every match is a disclaimer |
| Live scenario: fresh PostgreSQL 16 database, synthetic seed data, API and worker running | PASS; API probe 49/49, rate-limit probe 7/7 |
| Arabic and English screens | PASS; screenshots inspected |
| Source fidelity | PASS; the six phases are intact and the playbook `.docx` hash matches |

What the live scenario confirmed:
- **Closing a record:** an attempt to set a record to closed returns 422 from draft, active and on hold. The message names only product gate G6 and does not claim DG7 or any real approval. The record stays unchanged, a combined close-and-rename is refused as a whole, and no audit event is written for the refused close.
- **Access scoping:** a record outside the user's business-unit scope returns 404, and the admin sees no business records.
- **Updates:** a missing If-Match header returns 428, a stale one returns 409, and a request without a CSRF token is refused (403).
- **Defaults:** Asia/Riyadh and SAR are the defaults and remain configurable per record.
- **Branding:** the colour tokens are marked provisional and the header uses a provisional text wordmark.
- **Business-unit hierarchy:** a cycle is refused by both the API and a database trigger.
- **Language and assets:** Arabic renders right-to-left and English left-to-right, fonts load locally, and the screens made no outside requests.

**Requirements recorded:** REQ-S15-002, REQ-S15-005, REQ-S15-006, REQ-S16-001, REQ-S16-002, REQ-S16-004, REQ-S19-004, REQ-S19-006, plus REQ-PB-003. The assignment says to record those eight "exactly" but also mentions the playbook, §15 and §16 rows, so I used the same set as round 3; the live scenario covers REQ-PB-003. REQ-S16-003 is also a DG1 §16 row, and I left it out because it isn't in the listed eight.

**Things to note:**
- `pnpm install` failed in the sandbox because the pnpm store is read-only. I copied the store into scratch space and installed offline from the copy, with the same lockfile.
- The record's `source_commit` is HEAD `91936e6`, which I checked out. The manifest points to `642e6bf`; the newer commit only adds delivery records and gives the same candidate ID.

The review record matches the review schema, and every evidence path in it is an existing file. The disposable clone and scratch copies have been removed.

Files are in `docs/delivery/`:
- `reviews/DG1/round-4/domain-reviewer.json`
- `test-evidence/DG1/domain/round-4/` (logs, probe scripts and 8 screenshots)
